flashcards.back: The energy transferred when a force moves its object, calculated as force times distance in the force's direction, measured in joules.
How fast work is done, calculated as work divided by time, measured in watts: the same 200 J in 2 s is 100 W, in 10 s only 20 W.

flashcards.front: Energy gets used up when work is done.
flashcards.back: The car runs out of petrol and stops, so the energy feels destroyed. Energy is never used up: it changes form, like chemical energy becoming kinetic energy plus heat. In class, follow the falling mass: 98 J of GPE at the top becomes 98 J of KE at the bottom - the form changed, the total did not.

flashcards.front: A 2 kg book is lifted 1.5 m. Taking g = 10 N/kg, how much gravitational potential energy does it gain?
A machine does 600 J of work in 20 s. What is its power?

items.prompt: A moving car brakes to a stop. What happens to its kinetic energy?
items.answer: It changes into heat and sound; the total energy stays the same.

items.prompt: Which statement about energy is correct?
items.answer: Energy is never created or destroyed; it only changes form.

items.prompt: State the equation linking work done, force and distance.
A lamp changes electrical energy into light. Where does the rest of the energy go?
items.answer: It becomes heat, so no energy is lost overall.
